clue.text: Influence seen to take effect on child

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the effect-taking piece follows the child

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
to act is to take effect, as a drug acts

explanation.surface: Someone notices an influence working on a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: An impact is a strong effect or influence on something, so the noun swaps cleanly.

definitions.meaning: a target, the thing one aims at
one of the four Gospel writers, Matthew, Luke, John and this one

explanation.definitionFit: Both a target and the second Gospel writer share this name, one ordinary noun and one proper name.

clue.text: Declares girl's put on some weight

indicators.note: in a down clue, put on means placed on top of, so the girl comes above the weight

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name; the 's stands for 'has' or 'is' and gives no letter
ounces are a quantity of weight in imperial measure

explanation.surface: Someone announces that a girl has gained weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on some weight' reads as gaining pounds, but 'put on' places ANN above OUNCES in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce is to declare publicly, both verbs in the third person singular.

indicators.note: round means the attempt word goes around the island word

parts.note: a go is an attempt, a try
ile is French for island

explanation.surface: Instructions to travel around a French island's factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilery is a works where tiles are made, so it is a kind of factory.

clue.text: Made an obeisance — on the short side, perhaps

parts.note: curt means short or abrupt in manner

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word side might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Someone bowed slightly, perhaps being on the small side.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone short in stature; 'perhaps' is the anagram signal, and 'on the' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsey is a bow of respect, so curtsied means made a gesture of deference, past tense to past tense.

clue.text: Value talks before building stately home

indicators.note: before means the building piece comes after the value piece

parts.note: chats are informal talks
worth means value
a house is a building

explanation.surface: Someone prizes conversation ahead of construction work.
explanation.walkthrough: CHATSWORTH HOUSE is a famous stately home in Derbyshire, England, seat of the Dukes of Devonshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatsworth is one of England's best-known country mansions, an example of a stately home.

definitions.meaning: to book is to reserve, as with a table or seat
a team's substitutes or second string, the players held back

explanation.walkthrough: The second eleven is a sports club's second team, especially in cricket or football.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning arranges in advance and a noun for a club's back-up players.

clue.text: Soldier on a horse discovering spring (hot one)

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cavalryman comes upon a hot spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A spahi was a cavalryman of the Ottoman army or of French North African regiments, so a mounted soldier.

indicators.note: naughty suggests the letters of teaser misbehaving and being rearranged

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them

explanation.surface: A mischievous tease encourages people towards festive sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' rearranges TEASER into EASTER; 'urges' gives EGGS, as in egging someone on.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter eggs are chocolate treats given at one particular time of year, hence seasonal.

clue.text: Scales, for instance, somehow pulls near

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive in some other arrangement

parts.note: the fodder, which as printed has a stray S

explanation.surface: Weighing scales are somehow drawing closer.
explanation.walkthrough: Prunella Scales is an English actress, best known as Sybil in Fawlty Towers. As printed, 'pulls near' has a spare S, so the anagram works only from 'pull near'.
explanation.definitionFit: The actress Prunella Scales is an example of someone with this first name, hence 'for instance'.

parts.note: to box is to spar, so boxes gives spars

indicators.note: end picks the last letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Containers lie strewn about at the far end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like containers but is the verb: to box is to spar.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered or distributed, an adjective like the past participle used here.

indicators.note: can be signals that these letters may become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Even the gloomiest nun can let her hair down.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestrained and wild both describe behaviour free of control or restraint.

clue.text: Lay head taking sailor to speech workshop

indicators.note: head takes the first letter of the word Lay

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
oratory is the art of public speaking

explanation.surface: A lay leader brings a sailor along to an elocution workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is a room for scientific work, a workshop for experiments.

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the words metal container

explanation.surface: Powder kept in a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a fine mineral powder, such as talcum powder.

parts.note: O is round in shape
Leander is a famous rowing club at Henley-on-Thames

explanation.surface: A bush is growing around a boathouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Leander Club is a celebrated English rowing club at Henley-on-Thames; 'growing' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is a poisonous evergreen flowering bush, so a kind of shrub.

clue.text: A number of Muses hit target and achieve 180!

parts.note: there were nine Muses in Greek myth
to score is to hit the target

explanation.surface: A darts player hits the board and reaches the maximum 180.
explanation.walkthrough: In darts, 180 is the maximum score with three darts, which feeds the surface; a score is twenty, so nine of them make 180.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so nine times twenty gives the number 180.

clue.text: Crowd into taxi with nothing to dole out

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of dole are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: People pile into a taxi with no money to hand out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crowd into taxi' looks like the whole instruction, but 'Crowd' alone is the definition, as in 'the whole caboodle'; 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Caboodle, as in 'the whole caboodle', means the whole lot or crowd of people or things.

definitions.meaning: in maths and science, a value that does not vary

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for an unchanging value and an adjective for steadfast and loyal.
The word is both a verb for persistent fault-finding and a plural noun for horses, especially worn-out ones.

indicators.note: about places the writer's name round the crazy word

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe is the writer; the 's gives no letter
mad means crazy

explanation.surface: Someone is wild about an author's hair product.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomade is a scented ointment for the hair, a hairdressing in the sense of a hair preparation.

clue.text: What pandas eat after grass fires

parts.note: bamboo is a giant woody grass
to fire a gun is to shoot it, so fires gives shoots

explanation.surface: Food for pandas comes after grass fires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fires' looks like blazes, but it is the verb: fires a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant pandas live almost entirely on young bamboo stems, so this is their diet.

clue.text: Game for singer with nothing on

parts.note: Bing Crosby was a famous crooner
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A game for a singer who has no clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a numbers game of chance played with cards, so it is a game.

clue.text: Study early beginning of small valley

parts.note: a den is a private study or room

indicators.note: beginning of takes the first letter of early

explanation.surface: Early study of the start of a little valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A dene is a narrow wooded valley, a dialect word in northern England.

indicators.note: to means the rearranged piece is joined on to the doctor

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

indicators.note: about means the letters of dean are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grumbled about a college dean to a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges DEAN as ANED, attached to MO.
explanation.definitionFit: To moan is to complain, past tense to past tense.

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
to vow is to swear solemnly

explanation.surface: A girl took an oath when she was turned away.
explanation.definitionFit: Unavowed means not openly acknowledged or confessed, hence not admitted.

clue.text: Two novices see conversion of Alpine native

parts.note: a tyro is a beginner
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

indicators.note: conversion of says the letters of see are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A pair of beginners watch a mountain dweller change faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion of' rearranges SEE as ESE; a Tyrolese comes from the Tyrol in the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tyrolese is a person from the Tyrol, an Alpine region of Austria and Italy.

indicators.note: to means the allowed piece is joined on after the observer piece

parts.note: an eye is an organ that observes
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A gap in the rules was granted to a watcher.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small hole, and a loophole in its old sense is a small opening in a wall.
